key_insight: An algorithmic stability framework bounds expected catastrophic forgetting under SGD by tracking sample-perturbation propagation and cumulative gradient alignment across tasks.
engineering_relevance: The bounds clarify how dataset size, updates per task, task count, and learning-rate schedules influence forgetting in continual-learning systems.
method: Decompose forgetting into intra-task and cross-task generalization gaps plus empirical forgetting.
Track sample perturbations under constant, task-restarted decaying, and continuously decaying learning rates.
Bound empirical forgetting using cumulative gradient alignment without requiring convexity.
evidence_signal: Experiments on Split CIFAR-100 and Split MiniImageNet examine the empirical implications of the theoretical findings.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative results, so it does not establish which learning-rate schedule performs best in practice.
paper_title: Fine-Grained Analysis of Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Learning via Algorithmic Stability
